evidencePolicy.searchIndex: Used only to discover candidate articles. Search result text is not accepted as claim evidence.
evidencePolicy.openedOriginal: Each claim below was checked against the opened PMC full-text HTML at the listed section/line locators.
evidencePolicy.interpretation: Paraphrased anatomical claims remain separate from source wording; no human review or source-asset approval is inferred.

sources.title: Branching Patterns and Anatomical Course of the Common Fibular Nerve
sources.version: PMC full-text HTML of the published article; publisher-file comparison not performed.
sources.accessMethod: Opened full-text HTML directly; source text reviewed in Introduction, Materials and Methods, and Results.
sources.discoveryRole: Search index was not used as evidence.
sources.licenseObserved: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International stated on article page.

claims.claim: The article describes the common fibular nerve as a sciatic division that courses by the biceps femoris tendon around the fibular head, and later separates into deep and superficial fibular nerves.
claims.locator: Introduction, PMC HTML lines 121-123. This paragraph is literature synthesis; exact left/right source-object parent links were separately checked in the pinned source inventory.
claims.use: Branch hierarchy cross-check only; no individual branch point, course coordinates, or universal geometry.

claims.claim: The cadaveric series reports both a cross-over and a posterior course at the fibular head, so a single source curve cannot be treated as a universal course.
claims.locator: Abstract lines 107-116; Materials and Methods lines 135-149; Results lines 154-170.
claims.use: Supports retaining nerve geometry as unresolved until object-specific evaluated course and variation policy are validated.

sources.title: Anatomical study of fascial and aponeurotic bands in the anterolateral leg
sources.publication: Anatomy & Cell Biology. 2025;58(3):373-378. Published 2025-07-03; issue date 2025-09-30.
sources.version: PMC full-text HTML of the published article; publisher-file comparison not performed.
sources.accessMethod: Search result used only for discovery; opened full-text HTML and checked Anatomy, Methods, Results, and Discussion.
sources.discoveryRole: Search snippet not used to accept any claim.
sources.licenseObserved: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International stated on article page.

claims.claim: The article describes the common fibular nerve as the lateral sciatic division, then the deep and superficial fibular nerves as its terminal branches.
claims.locator: Anatomy, PMC HTML lines 193-197; Discussion line 299.
claims.use: General branch topology cross-checked against exact source parent-object pointers; not a source-side or geometry claim.

claims.claim: The authors dissected 52 lower-limb sides, including 27 right and 25 left, and observed multiple deep fibular branching patterns and recurrent articular branches to tibialis anterior in a subset.
claims.locator: Materials and Methods lines 207-229; Results lines 272-278; side summary lines 294-302.
claims.use: Supports bilateral relation scope and warns that a static un-evaluated curve cannot establish variant branch geometry or exclusive muscle supply.

sources.title: Anatomical study of the innervation of the tibialis anterior muscle and its relationship with myofascial trigger points
sources.version: PMC full-text HTML of the published article; publisher-file comparison not performed.
sources.accessMethod: Opened full-text HTML directly; checked Abstract, Anatomical technique, Results, and figure captions.
sources.discoveryRole: No search snippet used as evidence.
sources.licenseObserved: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International stated on article page.

claims.claim: The authors dissected 20 tibialis anterior muscles from 12 cadavers, followed deep fibular nerve branches to the muscle, and exposed/mapped their entry points; both right- and left-side measurements are reported.
claims.locator: Abstract/method summary, PMC HTML lines 127-138; Anatomical technique lines 165-173; side comparisons lines 267-280.
claims.use: Supports presence of a deep-fibular-to-tibialis-anterior motor-entry relation on matched sides. It does not establish exclusive supply, the complete course, or a model-specific coordinate/entry point.

notAdopted: No source curve coordinates, evaluated topology, pose binding, target-frame registration, or object-specific anatomical course was accepted.
No exact Korean nerve display term was established in this task; Korean name fields remain null.
No human review, public redistribution right, diagnosis, treatment, or needling claim was created.
